result.title: Rubric Curriculum RL: Exploiting the Generation-Verification Gap in Non-Verifiable Domains
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has led to significant gains in math and code generation. Extending these gains to open-ended domains remains challenging: ground-truth verification is unavailable, human annotation is expensive, and learned reward models are prone to reward hacking. The generation-verification gap, where judging good outputs is easier than producing them, offers a potential path to improvement. However, rubric-based judges are often imprecise and stationary, so policies can overfit or reward hack them. We introduce Rubric Curriculum RL (RcRL), which exploits this gap without new data, human annotations, or stronger teacher models. We combine pairwise preferences over rollouts with a curriculum over rubric criteria, yielding a more discriminative signal than absolute scoring and a non-stationary objective. Whereas baselines plateau within a few hundred steps, RcRL preserves output entropy and keeps improving past 1000 steps. On creative writing, RcRL achieves a 70.5% human win rate against the base model, with gains across benchmarks and judges. On HealthBench, RcRL improves over the base model by 14.6% (full set) and 25.4% (consensus subset), outperforming all training baselines, including instance-specific rubrics.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Rubric Curriculum RL（RcRL），在无真值开放域中把 rollout 之间的成对偏好与 rubric 准则课程结合，构造更具区分度且非平稳的奖励信号，避免策略对固定评判器过拟合并保持输出熵，在创意写作与 HealthBench 上优于基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其利用「生成难、验证易」的差距、并以 curriculum 缓解固定评判器被 reward hack 的思路，可能为 LVR 中难以逐步核验的 latent 轨迹监督与验证器过拟合提供训练信号设计线索，尚需核查能否迁移到多模态视觉推理。
